papers.title: Tailoring microstructure and properties of Ti-6Al-4V from piston-based material extrusion through hot isostatic pressing
papers.abstract: Piston-based material extrusion (PEX) is an additive manufacturing technology that enables the processing of metal injection moulding (MIM) feedstock to form green parts. The extrusion process does not require moulds and hence is a competitive alternative for the shaping of MIM process routes, offering short lead times and cost-efficiency for lower lot sizes, while integrating into the remaining process chain and equipment. This paper focuses on the microstructure and properties of Ti-6Al-4V fabricated by PEX and followed by a subsequent hot isostatic pressing (HIP) step for parts requiring superior density and mechanical properties. The HIP process is performed using standard as well as high-purity conditions (Quintus Purus ® ). After sintering, a globular, mostly α microstructure is observed. A subsequent HIP followed by rapid quenching transforms the microstructure to a bi-modal state. A similar effect on microstructure is observed for the Quintus Purus ® HIP; however, the formation of α-case on the part surface is avoided. While the mean density of the sintered parts is 97.2%, HIP leads to an increase to 98.9–99.3% with the remnant porosity mainly stemming from open, connected pores. Although the sintered specimens already fulfil the industrial requirements, the Quintus Purus ® HIP leads to a slight increase in yield and ultimate tensile strength at minimal reduction of elongation. The standard HIP shows the same but slightly more pronounced trend. The results show that by a careful design of the specific HIP conditions, the microstructure and properties can be tailored for a specific application.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索热等静压（HIP）作为Ti-6Al-4V活塞挤出成形件的后处理工艺
summary_zh.method: 采用标准和高纯度HIP条件对烧结件进行致密化和组织调控
summary_zh.result: HIP将密度提升至99%以上，抗拉强度略有提高而延伸率轻微下降

summary_en.motivation: To investigate hot isostatic pressing (HIP) as a post-processing route to densify and tailor the microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti-6Al-4V produced by piston-based material extrusion.
summary_en.method: Standard and high-purity HIP (Quintus Purus) conditions were applied to sintered green parts, followed by characterization of microstructure, density, and tensile properties.
summary_en.result: HIP increased density from 97.2% to 98.9–99.3%, transformed the microstructure to a bimodal state, and slightly improved yield and ultimate tensile strength at a minimal reduction in elongation.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via density measurements (Archimedes method) and tensile testing according to ASTM standards.
